title: Private Deploy Live-tail & Debugging Runbook
author: Priya Nambiar
content:
Purpose:
This runbook documents the standard operator procedures for live-tailing, real-time debugging, and safe mitigation of incidents in Private (VPC / on-prem) Redwood deployments. It is written for on-call SREs and field operators who need to quickly triage runtime issues, capture evidence, and perform controlled mitigations or rollbacks without breaching customer isolation guarantees.

Scope:
- Applies to all Private (VPC and on-prem) tenants running the Redwood runtime (services: ri-runtime, ri-operator, ri-control-plane)
- Covers user-visible latency/regressions, quota saturation, model swap failures, KV-cache regressions, GPU / node degradation, and telemetry gaps
- Does NOT cover long-term capacity planning or procurement activities (see tenant-capacity docs)

Owner & Escalation:
- Primary owner: Private Deployments Ops (oncall: private-deploy-sre)
- Secondary: Runtime Engineering
- Escalation path: oncall -> private-deploy-team lead -> service-owner (runtime@redwood.ai)

SLOs and Detects (Reference thresholds):
- Generation p95 latency (end-to-end): target < 350ms; alert if p95 > 700ms for 5m
- Token throughput drop: alert if aggregate tokens/s drops > 60% vs baseline for 3m
- KV cache hit ratio: target >= 0.65; alert if < 0.4 for 10m
- Request error rate: alert if 5xx rate > 1% for 5m or 4xx surge indicating broken client integration
- Telemetry heartbeat: control-plane heartbeat missing for > 3m -> page oncall

Quick Triage Checklist (first 10 minutes):
1) Validate page details & scope: tenant, region, time, customer impact (latency vs errors).
2) Confirm incident on observability: check Prometheus, Grafana dashboards (Tenant / Model / Node breakdown).
3) Live-tail runtime logs (ri-runtime) and operator logs (ri-operator) for the tenant.
4) Check resource health: GPU (nvidia-smi), node disk, memory, and network queue depth.
5) If issue is a model swap or deploy, verify artifact availability and model-serving logs (model-loader).
6) If degradation persists after 15 min, escalate and open an incident channel; gather evidence (traces, tail logs, config snapshot).

Primary Observability Sources (locations & metrics):
- Prometheus metrics: ri_runtime_request_latency_seconds_bucket, ri_runtime_request_errors_total, ri_kvcache_hits_total / ri_kvcache_misses_total, ri_token_throughput_total, node_gpu_utilization_percent
- Dashboards: Grafana -> "Private Deploy - Tenant Overview", "Runtime - Model Latency", "KV Cache - Health"
- Tracing: Jaeger UI at https://jaeger.internal.redwood.ai (service: ri-runtime, operations: Generate/Stream/LoadModel)
- Logs:
  - Operator logs: /var/log/ri/ri-operator.log (or systemd journal: systemctl status ri-operator)
  - Runtime logs: /var/log/ri/ri-runtime.log
  - Model loader: /var/log/ri/model-loader.log
- Field CLI: rictl (used to query tenant state, toggle safemode, fetch runtime snapshots)

Common Commands (examples):
- Tail runtime logs for tenant "tenant-acme":
  sudo journalctl -u ri-runtime | grep tenant-acme -A 200 -n

- Query Prometheus for current p95 for tenant (example):
  curl -s 'https://prometheus.internal/api/v1/query?query=histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(ri_runtime_request_latency_seconds_bucket{tenant="tenant-acme"}[5m])) by (le))' | jq

- Check KV cache hit ratio:
  curl -s 'https://prometheus.internal/api/v1/query?query=(sum(rate(ri_kvcache_hits_total{tenant="tenant-acme"}[5m])) / sum(rate(ri_kvcache_misses_total{tenant="tenant-acme"}[5m])) )' | jq

- Get operator-managed deployment status: rictl tenant status tenant-acme --output json
- Trigger safemode (see Safemode section): rictl tenant safemode enable tenant-acme --reason "oncall-latency-spike" --actor $USER

Evidence Collection (required for any mitigation):
- Capture 5m traces around incident start from Jaeger, include request ids.
- Prometheus snapshot of relevant metrics (p95, errors, throughput, KV hit ratio, node GPU util).
- Tail of the three logs above (operator/runtime/model-loader) covering -5m to +5m of incident window.
- rictl tenant snapshot tenant-acme > snapshot-<timestamp>.json

Detailed Playbook (by symptom):
A) High latency (p95 > 700ms) with low error rate
1) Check runtime CPU/GPU saturation: top / nvidia-smi on affected nodes. If GPU saturating (>95% utilization sustained), check for model inference loops or runaway requests.
2) Inspect batching backlog: rictl tenant backlog tenant-acme --nodes. If backlog grows and latency increases, consider temporary increase of worker concurrency (rictl tenant scaling adjust --workers +1) or enable burst pool if configured.
3) If KV cache hit ratio is low, check kvcached logs and warm by replaying hot prompts (see kvcache warmup below).
4) If no resource issues, collect traces and escalate to runtime engineers for slow-path kernel debugging.

B) Error spike (5xx)
1) Identify error class in logs (OOM, model-mismatch, runtime panics).
2) If OOM on GPU process: capture core dump (if enabled), reduce concurrency and trigger safemode to route to backup model variant.
3) If model artifact load error: validate artifact integrity (sha256) on runtime: ls -l /srv/ri/models/<model-id> and compare against control-plane metadata. If mismatch, mark model unhealthy and initiate model rollback.
4) If 5xx caused by model evaluation regressions, consult product/ML for golden prompt set regression test before model rollforward.

C) Telemetry missing / heartbeat gap
1) Check ri-operator connectivity to telemetry-bridge: sudo systemctl status ri-operator; check /var/log/ri/telemetry-bridge.log
2) Validate network connectivity to control-plane endpoints (curl https://cp.internal.redwood.ai/health).
3) If telemetry is down globally for tenant, enable local collection: rictl tenant local-telemetry enable tenant-acme --ttl 24h; this stores buffered metrics for later upload and prevents immediate alert storms.

KV-cache warmup recipe (when cold-cache causes latency spikes):
1) Fetch top 50 heavy prompt prefixes from recent traces: rictl tenant hot-prefixes tenant-acme --since 24h --top 50 > hot-prefixes.txt
2) Replay prefixes against model-loader in read-only mode with low concurrency to populate prefix/KV: rictl kvcache warmup --tenant tenant-acme --file hot-prefixes.txt --concurrency 4

Safemode (controlled mitigation)
- Purpose: minimize customer-visible impact while preserving operational safety. Safemode disables non-essential features (autoscaling, aggressive batching changes, model swap) and optionally routes traffic to a fallback model variant.
- Activation: only by oncall SRE or with authorization from private-deploy-team lead.
- Command: rictl tenant safemode enable tenant-acme --reason "<brief-reason>" --actor $USER
- Recommended safemode actions:
  - Route to fallback: rictl routing set tenant-acme --model model-id:stable-quantized
  - Disable autoscale: rictl tenant autoscale disable tenant-acme
  - Reduce worker concurrency: rictl tenant scaling adjust tenant-acme --workers -2
- Deactivation: rictl tenant safemode disable tenant-acme --actor $USER --note "recovered"

Controlled Rollback Procedure (for runtime or model changes)
1) Confirm rollback criteria met: recent deploy timestamp within 60 minutes and correlated error/latency spike.
2) Gather artifacts to preserve: rictl tenant snapshot tenant-acme > rollback-evidence-<ts>.json; capture Prometheus snapshot.
3) Rollback runtime image (example): rictl deployment rollback ri-runtime --tenant tenant-acme --image ri-runtime:v1.29.2 --wait 900s
   - Monitor readiness: rictl deployment status --watch --deployment ri-runtime --tenant tenant-acme
4) For model rollback: rictl model set tenant-acme --model-id model-123-stable --version v2026-05-04 --wait
5) Verify post-rollback health for at least 15 minutes: p95 back within SLO, error rate normalized, KV cache stable.

Emergency node evacuation (severe hardware / noisy neighbor):
1) Mark node unschedulable: rictl node cordon <node-id> --reason "evacuation"
2) Initiate tenant relocation for affected tenants: rictl node evacuate <node-id> --tenants tenant-acme --grace 300s
3) Watch for safe handoff in operator logs. If evacuation stalls, contact field operator to power-cycle or attach serial console.

Post-incident: Evidence preservation & review - Preserve all snapshots and logs in incident storage: /incidents/<incident-id>/ (runbook step: rictl incident create --id <incident-id> --source oncall)
- File an incident review within 72 hours using the Incident Review Template (link below). Include root cause hypothesis, corrective actions (short and long term), and owners with timelines.

Safety checks & guardrails (do NOT run unless authorized):
- Do not manually delete model artifacts from /srv/ri/models unless instructed by runtime engineering.
- Avoid simultaneous scaling and safemode toggles across multiple tenants unless coordinated.
- For any rollback that touches customer data paths, notify security and legal (customer-impact evidence retention required).

Playbook appendices:
- Appendix A: Common rictl commands (cheat sheet)
- Appendix B: Trace and query examples (PromQL snippets for p95, KV ratio)
- Appendix C: Postmortem checklist and blameless review template

Appendix A (cheat sheet):
- rictl tenant status <tenant>
- rictl tenant snapshot <tenant> > snapshot.json
- rictl tenant safemode enable <tenant> --reason "..."
- rictl deployment rollback <service> --image <image-tag> --wait 900s
- rictl node cordon <node-id>
- rictl kvcache warmup --tenant <tenant> --file hot-prefixes.txt --concurrency 4

Appendix B (PromQL snippets):
- p95 latency: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(ri_runtime_request_latency_seconds_bucket{tenant="tenant-acme"}[5m])) by (le))
- kv cache hit ratio: sum(rate(ri_kvcache_hits_total{tenant="tenant-acme"}[5m])) / (sum(rate(ri_kvcache_hits_total{tenant="tenant-acme"}[5m])) + sum(rate(ri_kvcache_misses_total{tenant="tenant-acme"}[5m])))

Appendix C (postmortem template):
- Incident ID, Date
- Summary (1-2 lines)
- Timeline (Timestamps, actions)
- Root cause hypothesis
- Short-term mitigations completed
- Long-term corrective actions (with owners & ETA)
- Lessons learned

- Cold-start mitigation playbook: /confluence/eng-private-deployments/day-2-ops/cold-start-latency-mitigation-for-private-deploys-2026.json

Contact list (for escalation):
- private-deploy oncall: private-deploy-sre@redwood.ai (pager)
- runtime engineers: runtime@redwood.ai
- product/ML contact for model regressions: mlops@redwood.ai

This runbook is reviewed quarterly or after any major incident. For suggested edits, propose changes on the doc and notify the reviewers list.
